papers.title: Group classification and equivalence of two classes of evolution equations of arbitrary order
papers.abstract: We revisit the group classification of the $(1{+}1)$-dimensional evolution equations $u_t=F(u_n)$ and $u_t+uu_x=F(u_n)$ of arbitrary order $n\geq2$, where $u_n=\partial_x^n u$, and describe the usual point equivalence groups of the two classes. We recover the known contact equivalences between the three second-order equations with seven-dimensional maximal Lie invariance algebras and extend the hodograph construction to points where $u_x=0$. For $n>2$, the dimensions of the contact symmetry algebras distinguish the two classes. We give reciprocal transformations linking the two classes at order three and formulate a nonlocal classification problem. We also classify the extensions of the Lie invariance algebra of the Burgers equation in a wider class of Galilei-invariant equations.

papers.title: B\"{a}cklund transformations of the fifth Painlev\'{e} equation
papers.abstract: In this paper B\"{a}cklund transformations of the fifth Painlev\'{e} equation are discussed. The B\"{a}cklund transformations are applied to rational solutions of the fifth Painlev\'{e} equation, which are expressed in terms of the generalised Laguerre polynomials and generalised Umemura polynomials. Using appropriate B\"{a}cklund transformations, we derive non-unique solutions of the fifth Painlev\'{e} equation in terms of modified Bessel functions. Further it is shown that there are also rational solutions in terms of generalised Umemura polynomials for the same values of the parameters, which are not special cases of the modified Bessel function solutions. The relationship between solutions of the fifth Painlev\'{e} equation and solutions of the third Painlev\'{e} equation is also discussed.

papers.title: Oriented V-systems
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of an oriented $\vee$-system which gives a class of solutions of the oriented associativity equations generalising Veselov's $\vee$-system solutions of WDVV equations. An oriented $\vee$-system is a special configuration of pairs of a vector and a covector in a linear space. We show that the class of oriented $\vee$-systems is closed under taking subsystems and restrictions. We provide examples which include a multiparameter family related to imprimitive complex reflection groups.

papers.title: Renormalization Group Flow from 4d Chern-Simons Theory
papers.abstract: The four-dimensional Chern-Simons theory coupled with surface defects is known to realize two-dimensional integrable quantum field theories (QFTs). We discuss the renormalization group (RG) flow of such two-dimensional integrable QFTs from first-principles Feynman diagram computations intrinsically in the four-dimensional framework. We first derive the one-loop RG flow of two-dimensional QFTs realized by the four-dimensional Chern-Simons theory on $\Sigma \times C$ coupled with the order surface defects supported on $\Sigma $. Here, the affine Kac-Moody symmetry of the defects underlies the one-loop RG flow. We then derive the one-loop RG flow of the principal chiral model (PCM) without Wess-Zumino term, which is realized using disorder surface defects, within the Batalin-Vilkovisky formalism. We obtain the nontrivial one-loop RG flow of the PCM, reproducing its known asymptotically-free beta function, using two complementary methods: by explicitly evaluating one-loop Feynman amplitudes, and by computing an analogue of analytic torsion for four-dimensional Chern-Simons theory.

papers.title: A proof of Nakamura's conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove Nakamura's conjecture on the relation between the 2D Toda model and solutions of the Ernst equation, using the Pfaffian solutions obtained in our previous work arXiv:2610.27420.

papers.title: Calculating correlation functions in integrable spin chains from local conserved charges and currents
papers.abstract: We develop a simple algebraic method for calculating correlation functions in integrable spin chains. We introduce current minors, antisymmetrized products of local conserved charge densities and their currents, and prove that their expectation values are determinants of density and current mean values. Decomposing local operators into current minors, we derive factorized formulas for correlation functions in terms of current mean values, valid in any nondegenerate eigenstate. Applying the method to the spin-$1/2$ XXZ chain and, more generally, to every representation of the Temperley--Lieb algebra, we prove previously conjectured factorized formulas for short-distance correlation functions.

papers.title: On the equivalence of three extended Calogero--Bogoyavlenskii--Schiff models to the classical CBS equation
papers.abstract: We examine the three extended Calogero--Bogoyavlenskii--Schiff (CBS) models introduced by Wazwaz, Alhejaili, and El-Tantawy [Eur.\ Phys.\ J.\ Plus \textbf{141}, 1218 (2026)]. Explicit invertible point transformations map the first model, and generically the second, to the classical CBS equation. The third model is generically equivalent to CBS with an additional spectator coordinate absent from the differential operator. We identify the exceptional parameter regimes and explain the reported exponential dispersion relations through these transformations. These equivalences show that the proposed models do not, in the generic parameter regimes, introduce new point-inequivalent CBS equations or genuine four-variable differential coupling.

papers.title: Non-Stationary Difference Equation and Affine Laumon Space III: Generalization to $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$
papers.abstract: In a series of papers, we have considered a non-stationary difference equation which was originally discovered for the deformed Virasoro conformal block. The equation involves mass parameters and, when they are tuned appropriately, the equation is regarded as a quantum KZ equation for $U_q\bigl(A_{1}^{(1)}\bigr)$. We introduce a $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ generalization of the non-stationary difference equation. The Hamiltonian is expressed in terms of $q$-commuting variables and allows both factorized forms and a normal ordered form. By specializing the mass parameters appropriately, the Hamiltonian can be identified with the $R$-matrix of the symmetric tensor representation of $U_q\bigl(A_{N-1}^{(1)}\bigr)$, which in turn comes from the 3D (tetrahedron) $R$-matrix. We conjecture that the affine Laumon partition function of type $A_{N-1}^{(1)}$ gives a solution to our $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ non-stationary difference equation. As a check of our conjecture, we work out the four-dimensional limit and find that the non-stationary difference equation reduces to the Fuji-Suzuki-Tsuda system.

papers.title: Temporal Complexity Hierarchies in Solvable Quantum Many-Body Dynamics
papers.abstract: The influence matrix (IM) provides a powerful framework for characterizing nonequilibrium quantum many-body dynamics by encoding multitime correlations into tensor-network states. Understanding how its computational complexity relates to underlying dynamics is crucial for both theoretical insight and practical utility yet remains largely unexplored despite a few case studies. Here, we address this question for a family of brickwork quantum circuits ranging from integrable to chaotic regimes. Using tools from geometric group theory, we identify three qualitatively distinct scalings of temporal entanglement entropy, establishing a hierarchy of computational resources required for accurate tensor-network representations of the IM for these models. We further analyze the memory structure of the IM and distinguish between classical and quantum temporal correlations. In particular, for certain examples, we identify effectively classical IMs that admit an efficient Monte Carlo algorithm for computing multitime correlations. In more generic settings without an explicit classical description of the IM, we introduce an operational measure of quantum memory with an experimental protocol, and discuss examples exhibiting long-time genuinely quantum correlations. Our results establish a new connection between quantum many-body dynamics and group theory, providing fresh insights into the complexity of the IM and its intricate connection to the physical characteristics of the dynamics.

papers.title: Nonlinear long extensional waves in an elastic layer with irregular free surfaces
papers.abstract: The propagation of nonlinear long extensional waves in a compressible hyperelastic layer with irregular free surfaces is studied within the framework of finite elasticity. The free surfaces are traction-free and symmetric with respect to the middle plane, and their irregularity changes the local thickness of the layer by a finite amount over distances long compared with the wavelength. In a distinguished limit in which weak nonlinearity, dispersion and the irregularity of the free surfaces appear at the same order, a multiple-scales analysis of the two-dimensional boundary-value problem leads to a Korteweg--de Vries equation with variable coefficients for the longitudinal strain. The irregularity acts on the wave only through the traction-free boundary conditions and changes the balance between nonlinearity and dispersion along the layer. After normalisation, the combined effect of the material and of the geometry is carried by a single variable nonlinear coefficient, whose sign decides whether compressive or tensile solitary waves exist. For special choices of the surface irregularity, the evolution equation reduces to forms known to be integrable, namely the Korteweg--de Vries and cylindrical Korteweg--de Vries equations. For periodically irregular layers of iron and copper and for model materials, numerical solutions show that a localized pulse propagates as a solitary wave, splits into a train of solitary waves or disperses into an oscillatory wave train, depending on the material, while the irregularity of the free surfaces redistributes the amplitudes of the emerging solitary waves.

papers.title: Symmetric discrete Mikhailov models
papers.abstract: The discrete Mikhailov model of [1] lacks conjugation symmetry, which prevents a direct reduction to the discrete Fokas--Lenells (dFL) equation and restricts the study of its solution structure. Revisiting the Cauchy matrix scheme, we construct four families of fully conjugation-symmetric discrete Mikhailov models by combining the equivalent relations of the auxiliary quantities pairwise. All of these models reduce to the symmetric semi-discrete and continuous Mikhailov models via a two-step continuum limit. The local reduction $\nu=\mu^{*}$ and the nonlocal reduction $\nu=\mathrm{i}\mu_{-}^{*}$ then give four families of local and of nonlocal dFL equations, for which exact Cauchy matrix solution schemes are established: the AKNS-type scheme for the local case, and both the AKNS- and KP-type schemes for the nonlocal case. We further characterize the dynamics of the obtained solutions in detail.

papers.title: Higher-Rank Connections and Deformed Schr\"odinger Operators
papers.abstract: We study the connection problem for a class of linear differential equations of order $N$ closely related to the Baxter equation of the quantum Toda chain. The space of solutions is $N$-dimensional and several linearly independent solutions decay at each singularity, leading to a rich structure of boundary value problems. We derive the weakest quantization conditions compatible with decaying behavior at both singularities, and formulate these conditions in terms of the associated monodromy data. In doing so, we prove the quantization conditions predicted by the topological string/spectral theory duality for a family of deformed Schr\"odinger equations. More generally, our results point to a hierarchy of spectral problems interpolating between the minimal conditions studied here and the maximally decaying boundary conditions of the $N$-particle quantum Toda chain.

papers.title: The N-soliton solution formula for the Kaup--Kupershmidt equation
papers.abstract: An explicit formula is presented for the $\mathbf N$-soliton solution to the Kaup--Kupershmidt equation, for any positive integer $\mathbf N,$ by using the input data set consisting of $\mathbf N$ distinct positive $p_j$-values and $\mathbf N$ arbitrarily chosen positive $c_j$-values. The formula is derived from the solution to the inverse scattering problem for a third-order linear operator in the reflectionless case with the $p_j$-values related to the bound-state poles of a transmission coefficient and the $c_j$-values related to the bound-state dependency constants. It is indicated how the formula is constructed from the solution to a Riemann--Hilbert problem and from the solution to a Marchenko integral equation used in the formulation of the aforementioned inverse scattering problem.
